passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (“MD&A”) was prepared to provide a historical and prospective narrative on our financial condition and results of operations through the eyes of management and should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and the accompanying notes to those financial statements. The discussion and analysis of the 2024 to 2023 year-over-year changes are not included herein and can be found in “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Conditions and Results of Operations” in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024. Our MD&A is organized as follows: • Overview • Results of Operations • Segment Analysis • Core Performance Measures • Liquidity and Capital Resources • Environment • Critical Accounting Estimates • New Accounting Standards • Forward-Looking Statements OVERVIEW Corning is vital to progress – in the industries we help advance and in the world we share. With a 175-year track record of life-changing inventions, Corning applies its unparalleled expertise in glass science, ceramic science and optical physics, along with its deep manufacturing and engineering capabilities to develop category-defining products that transform industries and enhance people’s lives. Our materials science and manufacturing expertise, boundless curiosity and commitment to purposeful invention place us at the center of the way the world works, learns and lives. In addition, our sustained investment in research, development and engineering capabilities means we are always ready to solve the toughest challenges alongside our customers. Our capabilities are versatile and synergistic, allowing Corning to evolve to meet changing market needs, while also helping customers capture new opportunities in dynamic industries. Today, Corning’s markets include optical communications, display, mobile consumer electronics, automotive, life sciences, semiconductors and solar. Corning’s industry-leading products include damage-resistant cover materials for mobile devices; precision glass for advanced displays; optical fiber, cable and connectivity solutions for advanced communications networks, such as fiber to the home and data centers, enabling artificial intelligence and connections around the world; trusted products to accelerate drug discovery and delivery; and clean-air technologies and technical glass for cars and trucks. In the third quarter of 2023, we introduced our Springboard plan to grow sales and enhance our profitability base. We communicated a high-confidence plan to add $3 billion in incremental annualized core sales by the end of 2026 (as compared to our Springboard starting point), and in March 2025 we upgraded this high-confidence plan to $4 billion. We also set a core operating margin target of 20% by the end of 2026. The fourth quarter of 2025 marked the second anniversary of our Springboard plan, and we believe it has been a tremendous success to date. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: We operate globally in a rapidly changing economic, political and technological environment that presents numerous risks. Our operations and financial results are subject to risks and uncertainties, including those described below, that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, our ability to successfully execute our strategy and the trading price of our common stock or debt. The following discussion identifies the most significant factors that may adversely affect the Company. This information should be read in conjunction with Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Conditions and Results of Operations (“MD&A”) and the consolidated financial statements and related notes incorporated by reference into this report. The following discussion of risks is not all inclusive but is designed to highlight what we believe are important factors to consider, as these factors could cause our future results to differ from those in our forward-looking statements and from historical trends. Risks Related to Our Business Inflationary price pressures and uncertain availability of commodities, raw materials, utilities, labor or other inputs used by us and our suppliers, or instability in logistics and related costs, among other factors, could negatively impact our profitability Increases in the price of commodities, raw materials, utilities, labor or other inputs that we or our suppliers use in manufacturing and supplying products, components and parts, along with logistics and other related costs, may lead to higher production and shipping costs for our products, parts and components. Further, increasing global demand for, and uncertain supply of, such materials could disrupt our or our suppliers’ ability to obtain such materials in a timely manner to meet our supply needs and/or could lead to increased costs. Any increase in the cost of inputs to our production could lead to higher costs for our products and could negatively impact our operating results, future profitability and ability to successfully deliver on our strategy. Increasing our prices to our customers may cause certain of our customers to push out, cancel or refrain from purchasing our products, which could materially adversely impact demand for our products, and thereby also negatively impact our operating results, future profitability and ability to successfully deliver on our strategy. credit_strengths.text: Corning's revenue and operating income expanded sharply, with operating margin improving to the mid-teens, though still below the sector median. The Springboard plan targets further growth and a higher core margin, supporting cash generation. This scale and diversification across optical, display, automotive and life sciences underpin the credit profile.

Operating cash flow covers debt service comfortably, with interest coverage above six times and a current ratio indicating adequate liquidity. Net leverage sits modestly above the sector median but remains within an intermediate risk tier, leaving headroom before the next threshold. Cash balances provide a buffer against cyclical demand.

key_risks.text: The risk factors highlight inflationary pressures and uncertain availability of commodities, raw materials, utilities and labor, which could raise production and shipping costs. Passing these costs to customers may reduce demand, pressuring profitability and the ability to deliver on the Springboard strategy. This is a concrete margin risk for a capital-intensive manufacturer.

Debt maturities are heavily weighted to later years, but a notable current portion comes due within twelve months, requiring refinancing or cash repayment. With capex not separately tagged, free cash flow after capital spending is unclear, and buybacks absorb cash. Refinancing risk is manageable but warrants monitoring given the debt load.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating income covers interest expense multiple times over, and operating cash flow is substantial relative to debt, indicating solid debt-servicing capacity. However, the cash-flow-to-debt ratio sits in a middle tier, and without capex data, true free cash flow after investment is uncertain. This limits visibility on deleveraging pace.

The maturity profile is manageable, with the bulk of debt due beyond five years, but the current portion requires attention. Cash on hand and expected operating cash flow should cover near-term maturities. Still, the absence of capex disclosure prevents a full assessment of cash available for debt reduction after capital spending.

overall_credit_view.text: Corning's credit profile is intermediate, supported by improved operating performance, adequate liquidity and manageable leverage. The Springboard plan targets further growth, but execution risks and input-cost pressures persist. Net leverage is slightly above the sector median, and cash flow coverage is mid-tier, suggesting limited cushion for a downturn.

We view the outlook as stable, with capacity to service debt absent a severe demand shock. The main uncertainties are input-cost inflation, demand elasticity and the lack of capex disclosure, which obscures free cash flow. Deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth and disciplined capital allocation, including shareholder returns.

credit_strengths.text: 康寧的收入及經營溢利大幅擴張，經營利潤率改善至十幾個百分點的中段水平，但仍低於行業中位數。Springboard計劃旨在推動進一步增長及提高核心利潤率，支持現金產生。光學、顯示、汽車及生命科學領域的規模及多元化支撐信貸狀況。
經營現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋債務償付，利息覆蓋率超過六倍，流動比率顯示流動性充足。淨槓桿略高於行業中位數，但仍處於中等風險級別，在達到下一個門檻前仍有緩衝空間。現金結餘為週期性需求提供緩衝。

key_risks.text: 風險因素凸顯通脹壓力及商品、原材料、公用事業及勞動力供應的不確定性，可能推高生產及運輸成本。將這些成本轉嫁客戶可能減少需求，對盈利能力及實現Springboard策略的能力構成壓力。這對資本密集型製造商而言是具體的利潤率風險。
債務到期日主要集中在較後年份，但相當部分流動部分將於十二個月內到期，需要再融資或現金償還。由於資本開支未單獨標示，扣除資本支出後的自由現金流不明確，而回購吸收現金。再融資風險可控，但鑑於債務負擔，值得監察。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 經營溢利覆蓋利息支出多倍，經營現金流相對於債務而言相當可觀，顯示債務償付能力穩健。然而，現金流對債務比率處於中游水平，且缺乏資本開支數據，扣除投資後的真實自由現金流不明確。這限制了對去槓桿步伐的可見度。
到期結構可控，大部分債務於五年後到期，但流動部分需關注。手頭現金及預期經營現金流應可覆蓋近期到期債務。然而，缺乏資本開支披露，妨礙全面評估扣除資本支出後可用於削減債務的現金。

overall_credit_view.text: 康寧的信貸狀況屬中等，受惠於經營表現改善、流動性充足及槓桿可控。Springboard計劃旨在推動進一步增長，但執行風險及投入成本壓力持續。淨槓桿略高於行業中位數，現金流覆蓋處於中游，意味著應對經濟下行的緩衝有限。
我們認為展望穩定，在沒有嚴重需求衝擊的情況下具備償債能力。主要不確定性在於投入成本通脹、需求彈性及缺乏資本開支披露，令自由現金流不明確。去槓桿取決於EBITDA增長及嚴謹的資本配置，包括股東回報。
